Evolutionary and functional relationships between plant and microbial C1 metabolism in terrestrial ecosystems

Simplified graphical representation of: (a) the photosynthetic C1 pathway including 5,10‐methylene‐THF production from serine conversion to glycine and the oxidative C1 pathway via the formaldehyde–THF reaction in the chloroplast, as well as cytosolic methionine synthesis and the downstream S‐methylmethionine (SMM) cycle involved in phloem loading and methyl group transport to sink tissues; and (b) photorespiration, including 5,10‐methylene‐THF production from glycine decarboxylation and the oxidative C1 pathway via the formaldehyde–THF reaction. Also shown are three common microbial pathways for C1 compound assimilation: (c) the serine cycle, (d) acetogenesis, and (e) the ribulose monophosphate (RuMP) cycle. Key enzymes involved in C1 metabolism are highlighted by functional category: oxidative C1 pathway enzymes (orange), THF‐dependent enzymes (light blue), and non‐THF‐dependent enzymes shared between photorespiration and the microbial serine cycle (pink). Enzymes marked with an asterisk denote those for which protein sequences were used in the phylogenetic analysis across plants, algae, cyanobacteria, and methylotrophic bacteria (see Fig. 4)
